method: Greedy nonoverlapping reversible digraph tokenization, respecting word boundaries. Compare baseline (letters only), ch/sh and five most frequent within-word digraphs chosen independently per corpus.
middle_english_source: local hand-extracted Chaucer sample, not a representative language corpus
voynich_source: four early local EVA folio samples, ambiguous tokens excluded
limitations: A digraph token is a reversible recoding, not a demonstrated medieval cipher.
Entropy per token cannot be compared directly across tokenizations with different units per word.
Different reference genres, text lengths, and EVA glyph conventions confound language inference.
No plaintext, cipher key, or matched historical-language result recovered.
